title: Infants Sucking Pattern Identification Using Machine-Learned Computational Modeling
summary: Machine-learned models classify infant sucking patterns from artificial-nipple tongue-force measurements, enabling objective characterization of feeding behavior.
ai_technology: Sensor-derived sucking data are split into training/testing and cross-validation; 1D-CNN and LSTM performance is reported against other classifiers.

evidence.tested: Machine-learned models classify infant sucking patterns from artificial-nipple tongue-force measurements, enabling objective characterization of feeding behavior.
evidence.unknown: The result is limited to the reported dataset, experimental setting and validation in this study; broader generalization and real-world benefit are not established.
evidence.ai_role: Sensor-derived sucking data are split into training/testing and cross-validation; 1D-CNN and LSTM performance is reported against other classifiers.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
